newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market late report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market late report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds erased initial losses and turned positive, pushed higher by the Italian market, while the Spanish 10-year spread reached a record low, dealers said.
They said no fundamental reason was behind the late rush, apart from some short covering but said the medium term underlying trend remained positive.
"We're tracking Italian bonds in the belief that peripheral markets will benefit most in the short run," one dealer said.
Chartists added that the long bond future was heading for a high of 117.10, a key resistance point.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Treasury allotted six-month bills at lower yields of 4.988 percent versus 5.009 percent two weeks ago.
Although the marginal reduction, dealers said they were now expecting the Bank of Spain to reduce its official rate by 25 basis points as soon as next week.
They said the Spanish central bank could cut rates, especially after benign May CPI data, at its first repurchase operation after the close of Amsterdam summit.
The next repo is scheduled for Tuesday June 24.
